- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10-15 days of forecast horizon).
- Forecasts show gradual upward drift, but true prices often dip sharply after initial peaks, suggesting model fails to capture short-term volatility or downward momentum.
- Model underestimates sharp declines or “sudden drops” in price, particularly after high peaks (e.g., 97+ → 80s).
- Model overreacts to recent high prices, showing persistent upward bias even when true prices are falling.
- Model fails to anticipate sharp reversals or mean-reversion patterns, especially in the 10-20 day window.
- Forecasts tend to be smoother than actual price movements, missing abrupt corrections or “sudden spikes” in true outcomes.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — often continues upward trend even when true price is falling.
- Model overestimates the “recovery” phase after sharp declines, failing to recognize that prices often return to prior levels faster than forecasted.
